verdicts.quote: "The Google Ads API uses OAuth 2.0 for authorizing API requests. Both OAuth 2.0 user authentication flow and service account flow are supported."
verdicts.reason: Docs explicitly state OAuth 2.0 (user or service account) is the auth mechanism for API calls. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/rest/auth?hl=en))

verdicts.quote: "Brand verification required for Basic and Standard access: For new Basic and Standard Access applications, you must complete brand verification..."
verdicts.reason: Credentials are self‑serve to start, but meaningful production use (Basic/Standard) requires brand verification/review → app_review. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/ads/blog/posts/2026/09/new-onboarding-experience-for-google-ads-api))

verdicts.quote: "Create and update Performance Max, Search, Demand Gen, Shopping, Video, and App campaigns, budgets, and assets."
verdicts.reason: Coverage spans many campaign types and core objects across the product, indicating a broad API. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/get-started/introduction?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block))

verdicts.quote: "The Google Ads MCP server provides a standardized bridge to the Google Ads API."
verdicts.reason: This is an official Google‑published MCP server, so mcp = official. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/developer-toolkit/mcp-server?trk=public_post_comment-text))

verdicts.quote: "The OAuth 2.0 scope for the Google Ads API is classified as a restricted scope, which means that you should complete the OAuth app verification process before productionizing your application."
verdicts.reason: It’s buildable now with self‑serve OAuth/Test/Explorer, but production use is constrained by OAuth app verification and access‑level reviews → ready_with_caveats. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/productionize/secure-credentials))
